name: Momofuku Bossam (Korean Slow-Cooked Pork)
ingredients_verbatim: 3.5 - 4 kg / 7 - 8 lb pork butt/shoulder, bone in, skinless
1 tbsp kosher salt (for brown sugar crust)
7 tbsp brown sugar (for brown sugar crust)
2 1/2 cups scallions, thinly sliced (ginger shallot sauce)
1/2 cup fresh ginger, finely grated (ginger shallot sauce)
1 1/2 tsp light soy sauce (ginger shallot sauce)
why: Salt-and-sugar cured pork shoulder slow-roasted until fork-tender then blasted for a brown-sugar crust, shredded and served with two Korean sauces - a distinct, non-American shredded-pork dinner with no equivalent in the catalog (adds Korean spread to a pork pool that skews Mexican/BBQ). Published 626 cal / 67g protein / 18g carbs clears the band (under 650 cal, under 35g carbs) with an enormous 67g protein. PRICER-LANE VALUE: carries two genuinely board-absent signature ingredients - ssamjang (fermented soybean-chili paste, no board id) and sherry-vinegar (board has red-wine/rice/white/apple-cider/balsamic but no sherry) - flagged in unmapped to exercise the pricer queue. gochujang, green-onions, fresh-ginger, soy-sauce, sugar, brown-sugar, vegetable-oil (canola), salt all map. CAVEATS for the selector: (1) 626 cal is near the ceiling, so our label-accurate pork-shoulder row could push computed cal over 650 - medium confidence it survives our own gate; (2) the sugar cure + brown-sugar crust drive the 18g carbs, still under ceiling but not deep-low-carb; (3) 24-36h dry cure is prep-heavy though still batch-scalable. Structurally low-carb protein, no rice/bread base in the dish itself.
confidence: high on published nutrition (read from source card); medium on surviving our computed cal gate at 626; distinctness high
